evidence: Both open with ‘In the beginning.’ Genesis uses divine speech; John identifies the Word as the agent of creation.
‘Let there be light’ is fulfilled in the Light that shines in the darkness and is not overcome.
Humanity made in God’s image; the Word becomes flesh and tabernacles among us.
All things created through Christ, echoing the creative work of God in Genesis 1.
Adam as the first man; Christ as the last Adam and life-giving spirit.
The promised seed who crushes the serpent’s head; Christ as the second Adam.
The seed of the woman fulfilled in the Son born of a woman.
Paul explicitly cites the Abrahamic promise that all nations would be blessed.
Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness — foundational for justification by faith.
Abraham’s offering of Isaac as a type of God offering his only Son.
Jacob’s ladder; Jesus declares himself the connection between heaven and earth.
The scepter shall not depart from Judah; the Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered.
